name: What should I ask before hiring a contractor for walk-in shower installation?

mainEntity.name: What questions help identify whether a contractor can build a waterproof, long-lasting walk-in shower?
mainEntity.text: What questions help identify whether a contractor can build a waterproof, long-lasting walk-in shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before hiring a contractor, homeowners should ask questions that reveal how the shower will actually be built, not just how it will look. Good questions include what waterproofing system will be used, how the floor slope will be formed, whether the drain will be moved, how niches and benches will be sealed, and what happens if hidden damage is found. It also helps to ask who is doing the tile work, whether permits or inspections are needed, and how the contractor protects the rest of the home during construction. A strong contractor should be able to explain the full assembly from framing to finish and give clear answers about moisture control. If the response focuses only on tile selection or looks vague about waterproofing, that is a warning sign. The right hire should provide a detailed scope, realistic schedule, and clear process for problem-solving during the remodel.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask about waterproofing method, drain planning, slope, permit handling, tile experience, and how the contractor handles hidden damage. The best contractor should explain the full shower assembly, not just the tile finish. Strong answers about substrate prep and moisture control are more important than a glossy estimate.
